decisions.statement: A property's files are numbered from the first.
The first of a property's files is the name that property would carry alone.
Every file after the first carries a part section.
The name `partAt` puts together `heldIn` takes apart again.
The files of one property are named in order from the first.
The files of a property held uncommitted are named in that same order.
Naming stops at the first file that is not there.
A gap leaves the files past the gap unnamed.
Whether a file is there is answered by the caller rather than here.
A caller reading a property's files is handed each file's body once.
That caller answers what a file holds rather than whether that file is there.
A body is handed over as the file it was read from and that body together.
A file past the first that holds nothing stops the reading.
The first file holding nothing is passed over rather than stopping the reading.
Nothing here reads the index or the disk.

definition: the ordered files one property of a page is held in
